title: Where the Work Is
description: The shape of the accessibility job market — who actually hires for this, how in-house, agency and freelance routes differ, what adjacent roles this skill opens, what the work really pays, and how to find employers whose remote and async culture is real rather than a job-ad phrase.

title: Certifications and Proof
description: What each accessibility credential actually signals, what it costs to get and keep, why a portfolio usually beats a certificate alone, and how to publish real work — an audit or an open-source contribution — as proof, without doing it recklessly.

title: Getting Hired
description: How to handle the take-home audit task and its marking criteria, narrate an audit live under observation, defend a severity call without becoming rigid, decide what disability disclosure actually owes an employer, and read whether an employer would be a decent one to work for.

title: Sustainable Practice
description: Structuring accessibility work so it doesn't cost more than it pays — staging audits to a real energy budget, absorbing the emotional cost of repeated barriers, holding a boundary as the only disabled person in the room, declining unpaid education requests, and choosing clients who will actually act on findings.

title: Staying Current
description: Tracking WCAG versions and what actually changed between them, which assistive technology updates genuinely change findings, the platform and browser shifts worth watching, the communities worth being in, and a repeatable quarterly routine that keeps all of it on a fixed, sustainable time budget.
